name: caucasus_ecoregion_forest_cover
title: Caucasus ecoregion forest cover
abstract:
Caucasus Ecoregion Forest Cover derived from BaseVue 2013 (raster layer downloaded, merged, clipped to WWF Caucasus Ecoregion and converted into vector format, forest cover extracted).

BaseVue 2013 (accessible from ESRI Living Atlas at http://goto.arcgisonline.com/landscape6/World_Land_Cover_30m_BaseVue_2013) is a global, land use / land cover (LULC) product developed by MDA (US), derived from roughly 9,200 Landsat 8 images, 30m spatial resolution. The capture dates for the Landsat 8 imagery range from April 11, 2013 to June 29, 2014. The following 16 classes of land use / land cover are listed by their cell value in this layer: (1) deciduous forest, (2) evergreen forest, (3) shrub/scrub, (4) grassland, (5) barren or minimal vegetation, (6) not used, (7) agriculture (general), (8) agriculture (paddy), (9) wetland, (10) mangrove, (11) water: (12) ice/snow, (13) clouds, (14) woody wetlands (only continental US), (15) mixed forest (only continental US), (16) not used, (17) not used, (18) not used, (19) not used, (20) high density urban, (21) medium-low density urban.

Terrestrial ECOS WWF Over the past eight years WWF's Conservation Science Program (CSP) has developed a biogeographic regionalization of the Earth's terrestrial biodiversity. WWF term their biogeographic units ecoregions, which they define as a relatively large units of land or water containing a distinct assemblage of natural communities sharing a large majority of species, dynamics, and environmental conditions. Ecoregions represent the original distribution of distinct assemblages of species and communities. There are multiple uses for the terrestrial ecoregion map in WWF efforts to conserve biodiversity around the world.

abstract: No abstracThe economic and geographical district of Kalbajar-Lachin includes Kalbajar, Lachin, Zangilan and Gubadli districts. The economic area covers 6.4 thousand km2 and covers 7.4% of the country. The economic region is located in the south-west of the country, in the Karabakh volcanic plateau and in the basin of the Hakari River. The economic region has rich mineral resources, such as gold, mercury, marble, chromite, grinding stone, copal, genuine, perlite and is rich in mineral springs (Istisu in Kalbajar, Minkand in Lachin). Kalbajar-Lachin was once one of the livestock breeding districts of the country. Tobacco, grain, grapes, fruit, and cattle, sheep and bees were stored in these areas. The economy collapsed as all administrative districts entering the economic region were occupied by Armenia.

title: Reservoirs_of_Azerbaijan_Republic
abstract:
In Azerbaijan there are 61 reservoirs, the volume of each of them is more than 1 mln.m3. The sum volume of reservoirs consists of 21,5 km3. They have been created on the river channel (channel reservoirs) and on the bout-skirts of them (reservoirs, the out-skirts of channel). A majority of reservoirs are regulated by seasons and they are used for irrigation. Reservoirs, created on Kur, Araz and Terterchay rivers and HES (Shemkir, Mingechevir,  Yenikend, Varvara, Araz and Serseng) are complex water management objects and they are used for energetic, irrigation, water supply and other fields.
The biggest reservoir of republic is Mingechevir. It is exploited since 1953. It works in multiyear regulation regime. Kur river’s run-off is completely regulated on its lower reach, and submergence events are prevented.

name: river_of_azerbaijan_republic_1
title: River_of_Azerbaijan_Republic
abstract:
The stream of republic is consisted of 8350 rivers, the length of 2 of them is more 500 km, 22 rivers – 101-500 km, 324 rivers  - 11-100 km, the length of great part of rivers is to 10 km. Generally, rivers of Azerbaijan Republic belong to Caspian Sea basin. They are divided into three basins:
1. Rivers of Kur river basin (left and right tributaries of Kur river);
2. Rivers of Araz river basin (left tributary of Araz river);
3. Rivers, falling directly into Caspian Sea.
All of constantly falling rivers and partially drying rivers have high watershed area, but temporary falling rivers low watershed area.  Kur river is the main water source and the artery of Azerbaijan. This river flows through the territory of Turkey, Georgia and Azerbaijan. The common watershed area of Kur river is 188 000 km. 58 000 km or 31% of this area belongs to Azerbaijan territory. After the Georgian boundary the run-off norm of Kur river is 270 m /s or 8,52 km in Girag Kesemen point. But in Kur-Salyan outfall the average annual run-off is 445 m /s or 14,04 km.
The second main river of our republic is the right tributary of Kur river – Araz river. It flows through the territory of Turkey. Also it is a transboundary river between Turkey and Azerbaijan, Turkey and Armenia, Iran and Azerbaijan. The common watershed area of Araz river is 102 000 km2, 18740 km2 or 18% of this area is in the territory of Azerbaijan.
The mean multi-annual run-off is 121 m3 /s or 3,82 km3 in the Novruzlu point (Saatli) of Araz river. The river system of republic consists of rivers on three groups: transboundary, boundary and local rivers. Kur, Ganikh (Alazan), Gabirry (Iori)< Khrami, Arpachay and other rivers belong to transboundary rivers (flowing through the territory of two or some countries). Araz, Samur, Bolgarchay and other rivers belong to boundary river (between two or some countries). Local rivers forms and flows through the territory of republic.
According to the area of the watershed and the watery of rivers there are 2 large rivers (Kur and Araz rivers), 12 numbers of middle rivers and creeks in the republic. Only 4 of local rivers may be considered as the middle river.

name: The_Shaki_Zagatala_Economic_Geographic_Region
title: The_Shaki_Zagatala_Economic_Geographic_Region
abstract:
The Shaki-Zagatala economic-geographical region is a region of Azerbaijan. The Sheki-Zagatala economic-geographical region consists of the local executive power and municipalities. The region includes Shaki, Zagatala, Balakan, Oghuz, Gakh and Gabala administrative districts. There are 6 districts, 6 cities and 8 settlements in the economic region. 
The Shaki-Zagatala economic-geographical region covers 336 villages. Shaki-Zagatala has an area of 8,960 square kilometres (2,210,000 acres) and a population of 586,700 (2012). The territory is divided into three parts: the southern slope of Greater Caucasus, the Ganikh-Haftaran Valley and the Central Kur Highland (Ajinohur and Turud-Sarica plain, the mountainous part of Shaki). Qabala, Oghuz, Shaki, Gakh, Zagatala and Balakan are rayons within the region. 
The altitude ranges from 100 - 466 metres, the peak of Mount Bazardüzü, which is the tallest mountain in Azerbaijan and Russia. The region includes the following important rivers: Kish, Shin, Balakanchay, Katekh, Damiraparan, Mazim, Mukhakh, Ganikh, Ayrichay, Alijan and Turyan. Rich sources of thermal and mineral waters are available at Oghlanbulag, Gizbulag, Hamambulag, Budusshor, Aghbulag and Khalkhal. Nohur (Qabala) and Ajinohur (Gakh) are the major lakes.
The rayon territory is rich in minerals. Most of the copper reserves of Azerbaijan, 90 percent of the sulfur arthroplasty, 97 percent of lead, 99 percent of sinks are extracting in this region. Filizchay, one of the largest polymetallic deposits in the Caucasus region, is located in the region. There are gravel, sand and other building material resources in mountainous and foothills. About 27 percent of the Sheki-Zagatala economic region is forested.

title: Water_channels_in_Azerbaijan
abstract:
Beginning point of irrigation canals as Nagorna Garabagh and Nagorno Shirvan from Mingachevir water reservoir which take a role in irrigation of Kur-Araz lowland. The densest network of irrigation canals has been formed in Mugan plain. In this plain length of main canals and banks is more than 3000 km. 
	Samur-Absheron irrigation canal was constructed which takes its beginning point from Samur river and flowing to Jeyranbatan water reservoir and its length is about 190 km. Water of this irrigation canal is not used for only irrigation drying soil of North-eastern area of Absheron and Azerbaijan, also using providing peoples water need and for industry of Baku-Sumgayit cities.

name: Yukari_Karabagh_economic_geographic_region
title: Yukari_Karabagh_economic_geographic_region
abstract: Yukari Karabagh economic and geographical area covers Khankendi, Aghdam, Jabrayil, Fuzuli, Khojavend, Khojaly, Shusha and Tartar regions. The total area of ​​the economic region is 7248 km2. This is 8.4% of the country territory. Upper Karabakh is between the economic regions of Aran and Kalbajar-Lachin. In the south, Iran crosses the Araz River, bordering the IR. The main natural resources are polymetallic ores, building materials (marble, cement raw materials, limestone), mineral springs and forests. The population of the economic region is 628,8 thousand people, including 206,1 thousand people in the city. 6.8% of the country population lives here (2012). Plain relief of the economic region, abundant agroclimatic resources, water resources of the Kura River, and the fertile soil in the conditions of irrigation create favorable natural conditions for agricultural activities and settlements. Agriculture is of great importance in the Upper Karabakh economic and geographical region. Its main areas are viticulture, grain growing, fruit and cotton growing, melon and vegetable crops. In the economic region, cattle breeding is mainly developed in the dairy and dairy sector. The industry is based on the processing of agricultural raw materials.
